If the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides, the triangle is right-angled.
The hypotenuse is always the side opposite the 90° angle and is the longest side.

concepts.title: 1. Theorem & Converse
concepts.subtitle: Relating Side Lengths
concepts.summary: In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the two perpendicular sides. Conversely, this relationship can be used to test whether a triangle is right-angled.

points.text: Pythagoras Theorem: $a^2+b^2=c^2$, where c is the hypotenuse.
Converse Test: Arrange the sides so c is the longest, then check whether $a^2+b^2=c^2$.
Three Outcomes: Equality means right-angled; a smaller sum means the longest angle is obtuse; a larger sum means the longest angle is acute.

concepts.trap: Always identify the longest side before applying the converse. The largest side must be tested as c.

concepts.title: 2. Hypotenuse Identification
concepts.subtitle: Locating the Longest Side
concepts.summary: The hypotenuse is the side directly opposite the right angle. It is also the longest side of a right-angled triangle, regardless of the triangle's orientation.

points.text: Opposite 90°: Find the right-angle marker and look directly across the triangle.
Longest Side: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is longer than each leg.
Orientation Independent: Rotating the triangle does not change which side is the hypotenuse.

concepts.trap: The hypotenuse is not defined by being horizontal, vertical, or visually diagonal. It is defined by its position opposite the 90° angle.

concepts.title: 3. Altitude & Base Vocabulary
concepts.subtitle: Choosing Perpendicular Sides
concepts.summary: Base and altitude are perpendicular quantities used together in area calculations. Either leg of a right triangle can serve as the base if the other leg is then taken as the corresponding altitude.

points.text: Base: The side chosen as the reference side for the area calculation.
Altitude: The perpendicular distance from the opposite vertex to the line containing the base.
Flexible Roles: In a right triangle, either leg can be selected as base, with the other leg serving as its perpendicular altitude.

concepts.trap: Do not assume the hypotenuse is automatically the base or altitude. Base and altitude must be perpendicular.

concepts.title: 4. Slant-Height Relation
concepts.subtitle: Applying Pythagoras Inside a Cone
concepts.summary: A cone's radius r and vertical height h form the perpendicular legs of a right triangle, while the slant height l is its hypotenuse.

points.text: Hypotenuse: The cone's slant height l is the hypotenuse.
Perpendicular Legs: Radius r and vertical height h are the two legs.

concepts.trap: Do not use vertical height h where a formula requires slant height l, or vice versa. CSA uses l, while volume uses h.

pool.statement: A cone has radius 6 cm and vertical height 8 cm. Find its slant height. (Variant 4)

steps.strategy_question: Which quantity is the hypotenuse in the cone's right triangle?

option_details.explanation: The slant height connects the apex to the circular rim and is opposite the right angle in the axial section.
Radius is one perpendicular leg.
Vertical height is the other perpendicular leg.
Diameter is not a side of the relevant right triangle.

steps.rubric_text: Did you identify l as the hypotenuse?
steps.hint: The slant height is opposite the right angle.

revisit_topic.title: Slant-Height Relation
revisit_topic.tip: l is the cone's hypotenuse.

steps.strategy_question: Which equation results after substitution?

option_details.explanation: Apply l²=r²+h² using r=6 and h=8.
The two perpendicular quantities are added when finding the hypotenuse.
The relation uses squares.
The Pythagorean relation uses addition.

steps.rubric_text: Did you substitute the radius and height into the correct relation?
steps.hint: Use r²+h².

revisit_topic.tip: The two legs are r and h.

steps.strategy_question: Which check validates l=10?

option_details.explanation: 100=36+64, so the Pythagorean relation holds.
